rows.description: A teenager, often a daughter in many homes, is expected to help more than a brother and quietly notices the unfairness. Fair sharing of chores regardless of gender teaches respect and lightens someone's load.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise young cook washes hands, keeps raw and cooked food apart, watches hot oil and gas, and never leaves the stove untended. Learning the safe habits early prevents both burns and stomach trouble.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student in a hostel or rented room meets laundry, cooking, cleaning and grocery planning for the first time and is surprised by how quickly things pile up. Small daily habits prevent a large weekly mess.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A flatmate who keeps washing others' dishes feels resentment growing over small unspoken things. A simple agreed rota or a calm direct word works better than a slow silent grievance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, calm, resentment

rows.subtype: Routine that keeps a home running [Response]
rows.description: A practical adult keeps a few fixed habits such as cleaning as you go, a weekly shop and a set laundry day. Steady small upkeep beats occasional heroic cleaning and lowers background stress.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child in a railway station or fair holds an adult's hand and is anxious about getting lost. Knowing a parent's phone number and where to wait if separated gives safety that fear alone does not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, detachment, trust

rows.description: A teenager taking a bus or train alone feels excited and a little afraid, checking the ticket and stops repeatedly. Small independent trips build competence when the route and a contact person are agreed in advance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young traveller follows navigation blindly onto a wrong or unsafe road and only then looks up. Apps assist judgment but do not replace noticing what is actually around.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A student saving money picks the cheapest connection, then loses a night or safety to a missed change. Cheap and reliable are different, and wise travellers weigh the hidden cost of delay.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A prepared traveller keeps tickets, ID copies and important contacts in two places, arrives early and has a plan if a train or flight is missed. Preparation is what turns disruption into inconvenience.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
